lines.content: description: Enforce the SE-EDU Git conventions for this project, including imperative commit subjects, informative bodies, and professional commit hygiene.
Follow the SE-EDU Git conventions for this project whenever creating or updating git history. Use the guide at https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/git.html as the required baseline.
1. Every commit must have a subject line written in the imperative mood.
- Examples: `Add README.md`, `Update task parser`, `Fix task list limit`
- Avoid past tense or gerund subjects like `Added README.md` or `Adding README.md`
2. Capitalize the first letter of the subject line.
3. Do not end the subject with a period.
4. Keep the subject concise: ideally under 50 characters and never over 72 characters.
5. Use a scope or category prefix only when it improves clarity.
6. For non-trivial commits, include a body separated from the subject by a blank line.
- Keep the body within about 72 characters per line
- Explain what changed and why, not how it was implemented in detail
7. Structure the body to explain the motivation, impact, and intent of the change.
All future git commits in this repository must follow this standard. Do not create commit messages that violate the SE-EDU Git conventions.
description: Enforce the SE-EDU Java coding standard (basic + intermediate) for all Java code in this project, including naming, layout, statements, and documentation conventions.

Follow the SE-EDU Java coding standard for this project at all times. In particular, apply the rules in the intermediate guide at https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html and use the Google Java Style Guide for cases not explicitly covered there.
1. Package names must be all lowercase and use logical group names.
2. Class, enum, and interface names must be nouns and use PascalCase.
3. Method names must be verbs and use camelCase.
4. Variable and parameter names must be camelCase.
5. Constant names must be uppercase with underscores.
6. Keep code layouts consistent and readable:
- keep braces consistent with standard Java style
- keep related fields, constructors, and methods grouped logically
7. Write clear, purposeful code comments and JavaDoc:
- document public classes and non-trivial public/protected methods
- document non-trivial private methods and helper logic
- keep comments factual and useful, not repetitive
8. Prefer descriptive, intention-revealing names over short cryptic names.
- avoid single-letter variable names except in very small loop indices
9. Do not introduce code that ignores these rules or uses project-local naming conventions that conflict with the SE-EDU standard.
All Java files in this repository must follow this standard. If code or generated changes violate these rules, fix the code before considering the task complete.
description: Run UI-style acceptance tests for the chatbot CLI by feeding command lists to the program, matching stdout against expected output, and recording the exact console transcript.
Use this skill when the current code change affects the chatbot's interactive CLI behavior and you need to validate output against a written test plan.
1. Update `test/ui-test-plan.md` when the behavior or expected output changed.
2. Run the UI test script from the repository root:
- run the app once per test case
- feed the case input as stdin
- compare the actual stdout to the expected output exactly
- print the console input and output for the test session
- stop immediately on the first failing case and print both actual and expected output
4. If any case fails, report the failing case ID, the actual stdout, the expected stdout, and the command transcript.
The file `test/ui-test-plan.md` contains a JSON block defining the app command and the list of cases. Keep it in this structure:
"app_command": "cd /path/to/repo && javac src/main/java/*.java && printf '%s' '...input...' | java -cp src/main/java Sage",
The JSON is the source of truth for test execution; the surrounding markdown is for human-readable documentation.
